text: ‍DALLAS FED: Mexican economy gains momentum August 6, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The Federal Reserve's own Mexico update: GDP grew 6.1% annualized in Q2, exports are up 20% year-over-year, formal employment added 107,000 jobs in June, inflation down to 3.4%. And what does the Fed credit for resilient consumption? Minimum wage increases and universal pension transfers — 4T policy, in a Fed research note. 🔍 No editorializing, no "concern" — just the data the opinion pages keep skipping. • "GDP grew 6.1 percent annualized quarter over quarter" • "rising purchasing power from minimum wage increases and direct government transfers" • "total exports were up 20.0 percent"

‍BLOOMBERG OPINION: Mexico Is Winning the Trade War Through Hospitality August 6, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Bloomberg Opinion admits Mexico is winning Trump's trade war — but can only explain it as "hospitality." Smiles and patience, not the numbers: Mexican exports still largely sheltered under USMCA while Washington tore up the July 1 renewal deadline in favor of annual reviews. 🇲🇽 The author calls Sheinbaum's strategy a winner, yet frames it as a host's good manners rather than statecraft — after a year of "tariff chaos" coverage, the concession arrives as a compliment about courtesy. • "Smiles, cooperation and lots of patience" • "the Trump administration declined to rubberstamp a long-term renewal"

🇲🇽💵 <u>SUPERPESO CLOSES THE WEEK AT 17.13 — STRONGEST SINCE FEBRUARY</u>

The peso ended the first week of August at 17.13 per dollar, appreciating 0.41% on Friday and touching 17.08 intraday — its best level since February 18, per Banxico. Drivers: a sinking dollar (DXY -0.34% to 99.59) and July inflation cooling to 3.12% from 3.37% (El Financiero). While the US lurches from tariff threat to tariff threat, Mexico's currency keeps voting confidence.

🇲🇽🤖 <u>MORENA PUSHES ONE NATIONAL AI LAW — NOT 32 STATE PATCHWORKS</u>

Morena is moving to empower Mexico's Congress to legislate on artificial intelligence across the entire country, heading off a patchwork of 32 different state regulations. The goal: regulatory certainty for nearshoring and foreign investment, anchored in the Constitution so it survives changes of administration. The stakes, per the initiative: studies estimate AI could contribute up to $305 billion to Mexico's GDP by 2038.
banner: MORENA: ONE AI LAW FOR ALL MEXICO

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO RESTORES TIES WITH PERU AS BETSSY CHÁVEZ ARRIVES IN CDMX</u>

Peru's government granted the safe-conduct Mexico had been requesting for weeks for former prime minister Betssy Chávez — asylee in Mexico's embassy in Lima since the December 2022 coup against Pedro Castillo. A Mexican Air Force plane flew her out; she landed Friday morning. Sheinbaum announced the result: "With this, relations with Peru will be restored." No retreat on principle: "We will continue defending President Castillo — the new Peruvian government knows it."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PRI'S 'POLITICAL POLICE' SPIED ON EVERYONE — SHEINBAUM'S FAMILY INCLUDED</u>

Contralínea begins a series on the DFS files held by the National General Archive at Lecumberri: Mexico's defunct political police systematically surveilled dissidents and its own ranks alike — PRI members and even ex-presidents, the PAN, the left, writers, artists, diplomats, media owners and journalists. The espionage outlived the PRI era, ran through the PAN years, and intensified again under Peña Nieto. Part one: the surveillance files on Claudia Sheinbaum and her family.
banner: DFS FILES: PRI SPIED ON SHEINBAUM

text:
🇲🇽🌳 <u>MEXICO PLANTS 6.6 MILLION TREES TODAY IN ALL 32 STATES</u>

The first Jornada Nacional de Reforestación kicked off at 7am across the whole country: 235,097 people planting 6.6 million trees and plants of 302 species on 32,184 hectares, covering 621 municipalities, 1,632 agrarian communities and 17 protected natural areas. The annual event follows through on Sheinbaum's G20 pledge in Rio: "sow peace and life instead of wars" — put 1% of military spending into the largest reforestation program in history.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>SHEINBAUM: FORGIVING 'UNPAYABLE' MORTGAGES IS JUSTICE, NOT A RAID ON INFONAVIT</u>

Nearly 5 million Mexican families were stuck with Infonavit loans they could never pay off — the legacy of a housing fund that, in the President's words, "was really a business for a few." In Puebla, Sheinbaum answered the critics: "They say we're putting Infonavit at risk. Absolutely false. It's justice — people already paid for their homes." One beneficiary borrowed 89,000 pesos, paid back 246,000, and still owed 1.6 million. Her debt was wiped out entirely.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>US ALUMINUM LOBBY: KEEP TARIFFS ON MEXICO, T-MEC BE DAMNED</u>

The Coalition for a Prosperous America is lobbying Washington to keep — and expand — tariffs on Mexican and Canadian aluminum in the T-MEC review, rejecting any exemption for extrusions, tubes, structures and other manufactured goods. "Rules of origin are no substitute for real tariff protection," says CPA's Jeff Ferry Toomey. Free trade, it turns out, lasts exactly as long as Mexico doesn't compete. (El Financiero)
banner: ALUMINUM: US LOBBY WANTS MEXICO TARIFFS

text:
🇲🇽📊 <u>CDMX STUDY: WORKPLACE INCLUSION RAISES PRODUCTIVITY</u>

Ten years of Mexico City's Copred agreement with private business, and the receipts are in: 97% of signatory companies say their people work comfortably, 93.9% report operational improvements, 87.9% registered measurable productivity gains. Since 2019, 282 corporate policies reviewed. Copred's Geraldina González de la Vega: the evidence matters "in an international context where diversity, equity and inclusion policies face new challenges." While Washington wages war on DEI, CDMX proves equity pays.
